verdicts.note: Self-refers as 'a girl' throughout; female clearly supported.
'big normal comprehensive school' and explicitly not all-girls -> mixed.
'I'm in my 2nd year - at the end now' -> Part B/Year 2.
Civil engineering confirmed throughout.
Salary never cited as a draw; anti-money stance supports disagree, though quote is from job-prospects context.
Repeatedly stresses 'so general'/variety as main appeal -> strongly agree.
Quote is about jobs in other fields/breadth, not specifically maths+science without specialising; thin, downgrade to low.
'it's a good degree - and they're not sure they actually want to be it' matches construct exactly.
Bet implies she got A's in sciences and took maths/physics A-levels; agree defensible.
'I don't even know what that is' -> chose with little knowledge of the job.
Parents not engineers; only vague 'granddad...or something'; did not learn of engineering via family -> disagree.
Interests are sport/PE, dad never taught engines -> hobbies not technical -> disagree.
Parents 'didn't have a clue'; mother did not encourage engineering -> disagree.
'dad's not very engineering minded' -> father did not encourage -> disagree.
Careers advisor explicitly 'put the idea in my head'; named biggest influence -> strongly agree.
Physics teacher named as 'big influence' (role model/civil engineer) but no explicit encouragement; thin, downgrade to low.
No one discouraged engineering (mother only discouraged PE); 'thought it was a really good idea' -> no.
'I just wish we had more practical modules' -> level not just right -> disagree.
Repeated: modules 'so specific', hydraulics/maths 'not going to be any use' -> strongly agree relevance is hard to see.
Ambivalent: 'good degree' yet course boring and unsure about being an engineer; neither is a fair middle read.
'it's quite competitive on the course...you don't want to fall behind' -> agree.
Quote is about being favoured for ADMISSION/entry ('reason I got in'), not about getting more HELP IN CLASS; does not support this construct.
Group work with diverse people 'the way it's gonna be all your life' -> course develops interpersonal skills -> agree.
Personal tutor 'terrible...not a very good people person' -> very dissatisfied.
Mates biggest influence, 'get on with everyone fine' -> very satisfied with friends.
'so theoretical - that's a bad thing' -> dissatisfied with theory work.
Wants more practical modules -> dissatisfied with amount of practical work.
Design module 'so good...really fun' -> very satisfied with design work.
Mixed: enjoys good projects but free-riders annoy her, 'It's OK' -> neither.
'80% exams...wish they'd been worth more' -> coursework/exam balance not right -> disagree.
'doing the year out with the same company' -> yes.
'So I could have some money' as primary stated reason for sponsorship route -> strongly agree.
'getting more practical experience really' as a good thing -> strongly agree.
'get my foot in the door when I leave, without having to do interviews' -> improve job chances -> agree.
'more idea about...what field I want to go into' -> help decide future -> strongly agree.
'I know what the programme is...wouldn't have known otherwise' -> idea of what industry is like -> agree.
'you can do ok without being chartered' -> chartership not a driver -> disagree.
Factually has summer-placement work experience, but item frames it as a reason for NOT going on placement (she IS going); mapping strained, downgrade to low.
Believes placement effectively required as sponsored student ('if you don't then you're really bad'); hedged -> compulsory.
'liked the management aspect best...organise things' + site managing -> project management.
'going into site managing, being a site manager' -> managerial.
'involve a lot of travel', would 'love to' work abroad, 'I want to go travelling' -> very important.
Disparages money-obsessed site workers, distances self ('if you work for money what's the point') -> unimportant; mild hedge, medium ok.
'I like people to like me' re site role; interpersonal harmony at work matters -> important; somewhat about being liked rather than colleagues, medium ok.
